newsitem.title: USA: Daschle reverses self on US securities bill twice.
newsitem.headline: Daschle reverses self on US securities bill twice.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle reversed himself twice within a period of 10 minutes Thursday on whether a securities reform bill had passed.
Daschle announced at a news conference that a mistake had been made and the bill, reported passed Tuesday, had actually never been passed. He said that a mistake had been made.

Minutes after reporters rushed to file the news, his staff fanned out through press galleries to say that the South Dakotan senator had made an error. In fact, they said, the bill had indeed passed on voice vote as reported this week.
The major securities bill overhauls regulation of mutual funds and gives the Securities and Exchange Commission $20 million in additional funds to supervise investment advisers.

At first, Daschle told reporters, "I thought it had passed." He then said he learned later that Republican Sen. John Ashcroft of Missouri had objected and therefore, "it hasn't passed the Senate." The measure passed by a procedure called "unanimous consent" where no formal vote is taken.
A few minutes later in the press conference Daschle's staff came in and told Daschle that Ashcroft had later withdrawn his objection and the bill had in fact passed.
A perplexed Daschle looked at the reporters and said: "Never mind."
The press conference broke into laughter, but by that time the initial report had gone out that the bill was not passed.
